items.title: Helsing built an AI system that prepares targets for weapons systems and says every decision will carry a human name
items.summary: Helsing has unveiled Clarity, an AI platform that uses agents to distill sensor data into target recommendations for weapons systems, all under human oversight and European control. But experience from the Iran war, Gaza, and a near-miss involving China shows that the speed of automation and data fusion create risks that are hard to contain. items.title: Anthropic says AI is eroding Nvidia's CUDA lead, cutting an AMD chip switch from months to three days
items.summary: Anthropic claims it used AI itself to breach Nvidia's CUDA moat. The company's in-house model Mythos reportedly ported Claude to AMD GPUs in just three days, with almost no human intervention. Anthropic now runs Claude on four chip families and aims to cut costs and reduce vendor dependencies. items.title: US data brokers are selling half a billion dollars in RL training environments to Chinese AI labs
items.summary: US data brokers like Mercor, Surge AI, and AfterQuery are selling roughly half a billion dollars' worth of AI training data to Chinese labs, according to a ChinaTalk investigation. That includes the same RL environments previously built for OpenAI or Anthropic. At least nine firms are involved, and export controls barely apply. items.title: DeepL wants real-time translation to finally capture sarcasm and mood shifts
items.summary: DeepL Voice's real-time translations are about to sound a lot more natural. The company's new Aure model carries over tone, emotion, emphasis, and speaking pace from the original speaker's voice into the target language. items.title: Grok-built apps exposed patient data, plaintext passwords, and SpaceXSI's own sales pipeline
items.summary: Security firm Claroc found more than 35,000 Grok-built apps open to anyone without login, including patient data and confidential SpaceXSI documents. The cause: "Anyone with the link" was preselected as the default access setting. SpaceXSI took only its own 24 employee apps offline. The rest remain accessible. The article Grok-built apps exposed patient data, plaintext passwords, and SpaceXSI's own sales pipeline appeared first on The Decoder.

items.title: Enterprise sales push OpenAI's quarterly revenue to $10 billion, though it still trails Anthropic
items.summary: OpenAI grew its quarterly revenue 50 percent to $10 billion but is still burning more cash than it brings in. Adjusted operating losses climbed to $10.9 billion, while rival Anthropic operates far more efficiently on $17 billion in revenue. To close the gap, OpenAI is now fueling a price war for enterprise customers. items.title: UK regulator threatens universities with sanctions unless they adopt AI-proof exam formats
items.summary: England's higher education regulator, the Office for Students, says AI has made it "nearly impossible" to fairly assess student coursework. An investigation found that students are having ChatGPT write entire papers undetected, without being able to recall basic content afterward. items.title: OpenAI turns ChatGPT into a business directory with AI agents that handle customer questions
items.summary: OpenAI is opening up ChatGPT as a business platform: through a new Business Hub, companies can claim their profile, add product data, and track how users interact with them. "Business Agents" let eligible US e-commerce providers talk to customers directly inside ChatGPT. items.summary: Anthropic is expanding Claude with Sheets, Whiteboards, and Interactive Connectors, letting partners like Adobe and Atlassian embed their apps directly inside Claude. Anthropic says Claude Meetings, which can join calls and take notes, is coming soon. items.title: Nvidia's model GR00T 2 watches humans on video, then imagines itself as the robot
items.summary: Nvidia's new AI model GR00T 2 is designed to teach robots new tasks without laborious teleoperation. Instead, the system transfers human hand movements from videos to robotic arms, trained on about 400,000 hours of video footage. Success rates still vary widely, though, ranging from 10 to 80 percent depending on the task.
